headline: AMD's Lisa Su met Korean AI chip companies in Seoul to explore building systems that pair AMD processors with Korean AI chips.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: concrete meetings and plans, but no signed deal.
importance_line: Korean AI chip startups could gain a route to global customers and AMD another way to challenge Nvidia, but the talks are exploratory and the planned Korean research centre has no site yet.
summary: The Korea Herald reports that AMD chair and chief executive Lisa Su met Korea's deputy science minister and executives of 13 Korean AI chip, software and cloud companies in Seoul on Wednesday to discuss pairing AMD's processors with Korean chips built for AI inference (running trained models), with demonstration projects in Korea to test the systems. AMD also reaffirmed plans for an AI research centre in Korea by year-end with hundreds of researchers, and talks covered joining its open-source ROCm software, a rival to Nvidia's CUDA.
notes: Read in full (Korea Herald). Su was also expected to meet Samsung's chip chief; the report does not say that meeting happened.
